title: One Piece Creator Saved Netflix’s Live-Action Series With Big Change During Production
content:
It turns out One Piece creator Eiichiro Oda saved the production of Netflix’s live-action series adaptation with a major change to its budget and scripts as revealed by one of the showrunners behind it all. Netflix’s One Piece live-action series has been hailed as one of the most beloved adaptations in recent memory, and it’s because all those involved have seemingly been huge fans of the original work. And helping in that matter is the fact that the creator himself has been greatly involved with it as well.

Speaking with the Trash Taste Podcast , One Piece live-action series showrunner Steven Maeda opened up about how directly involved series creator Eiichiro Oda has been with the adaptation. Revealing that it took so long for that first season to get off the ground was because the scripts went through multiple versions with executives at Netflix threatening to cut the budget in half before Oda himself intervened , “This is not what I signed up to do.”

How One Piece Creator Saved Netflix’s Live-Action Series

As Maeda explained about the process, the initial drafts of the scripts were written for ten episodes for its debut season. But a new Netflix executive came to look at the scripts and noted “I like this, but it’s got to be way, way cheaper. We want you to cut the budget in half, and it’s going to be cut down into eight episodes now instead of the ten.” Maeda noted how the One Piece fans would not be happy with such changes because they couldn’t “afford to do the things that we sort of promised to do .” But they went back and tried for eight episodes anyway.

Maeda then explained how they went and re-wrote the season with eight episodes, but had to change some things due to the lower budget from Netflix, “I thought it was a very potentially good first season of television, but it was really getting farther and farther away from the One Piece storytelling. As a result, I was very worried they were going to pull the plug.” Maeda then explained that Oda read it and did not like it , telling Netflix “This is not what I signed up to do.” Netflix then reconsidered, and came back with the reveal that they were going to give the show the budget to do the version the team wanted to do.

What Does This Mean for Netflix’s Live-Action One Piece Future?

With this retooling of One Piece to the eventual version that made its debut, it proved to be a success enough that it was picked up for two more seasons. Maeda explained that the series was actually picked up for Seasons 2 and 3 at the same time, and that was partly due to the fact that Netflix wanted to reduce the wait time between each of the seasons to avoid the aging of the cast and other potential production wait times. Maeda is hopeful that the series is picked up for Seasons 4 and 5 in the future, but we’ll just have to wait and see what’s next.

One Piece: The Battle of Alabasta is currently scheduled to release with Netflix sometime in 2027, but no concrete release date as of this time. This is the third season of the series adapting the biggest arc yet, so it’s not quite clear if the live-action series will decide to end with this next batch of episodes. How have you been liking One Piece’ s live-action series so far? Let us know all of your thoughts about it so far.

title: Novelist Ryū Murakami Dies at 74
content:
There was a private funeral for family members.

Murakami was born in Nagasaki Prefecture in 1952. He made his debut with the novel Almost Transparent Blue , which sold more than 3.5 million copies.

Murakami's 1996 Love and Pop: Topaz II novel inspired the 1998 live-action film Love & Pop (pictured right), directed by Hideaki Anno ( Neon Genesis Evangelion ). GKIDS screened the film in North American theaters in February 2025, and it also releasing it on home video.

Murakami's other works include Coin Locker Babies , The World in Five Minutes From Now , Kyoko , and Tokyo Decadence . He wrote and directed film adaptations of some of his works. He was also an interviewer on the economic talk show The Cambrian Palace .

title: One of the Darkest Anime Returns With First Look at Next Big Movie
content:
One of the darkest anime franchises out there is coming back with a new movie release, and is gearing up with the first look at what’s coming next. There are plenty of dark anime franchises that have garnered a lot of attention over the years, but there won’t be one with as much impact as the anime adaptation for Akihito Tsukushi’s Made in Abyss . Throwing children into the titular abyss with deadly monsters, it’s no mystery why the franchise has had a ton of TV and feature film releases.

Made in Abyss is currently working its way through a new a brand new trilogy of planned feature film releases , and the first film of this trilogy is currently working its way through theaters across Japan as of this month. To celebrate the debut of the first film, Made in Abyss has confirmed that work has begun on the second major entry in the trilogy and has dropped the first look at some of the new characters and cast additions that fans will see in action. You can check it out below.

Made in Abyss Confirms New Movie Now in the Works

Made in Abyss: Mezameru Shinpi is currently screening in theaters across Japan , and is the first in a planned trilogy of new films now confirmed to be in production for the franchise. The new additions to the voice cast revealed with this new poster are Nana Mizuki as Srajo, Akeno Watanabe as Nishagora, Shunsuke Takeuchi as Yataramar, Nao Toyama as Sherumi, and Yume Miyamoto as Menae. The second film for this trilogy is now in the works as well, and will feature a returning staff and voice cast from the previous entry and TV anime series.

Made in Abyss: Mezameru Shinpi is directed by Masayuki Kojima for Kinema Citrus with Hideyuki Kurata handling the script for the films, Kazuchika Kise and Yuka Kuroda handling the character designs, and Kevin Penkin composing the music. Penkin also contributed to the theme song for the first film titled “Chain of the Abyss,” with Mori Calliope. Now with a second film continuing the trilogy further, it seems like the franchise’s return has been deemed a success enough to keep it all going in the near future.

What to Know for the Made in Abyss Film Trilogy

Made in Abyss: Mezameru Shinpi also features a returning voice cast from the TV anime with the likes of Mariya Ise as Reg, Miyu Tomita as Riko, Shiori Izawa as Nanachi, and Misaki Kuno as Faputa. Other new additions revealed in the first film include Sumire Morohoshi as Tepaste and Takanori Hoshino as Cravagli. Unfortunately for fans outside of Japan at the moment, no potential international release plans have been revealed for the trilogy as of this time.

Made in Abyss is a rather dark series that puts children in some very real danger, and it’s been such a hit with fans that there has not only been adapted into two seasons of the TV series, but a few feature film releases continuing the story too. Now this new trilogy is set to take things even further. But are you going to check out the Made in Abyss trilogy if you get the chance? Let us know all of your thoughts about it in the comments!

title: After 22 Years, Bleach Anime Ends With Final Episode Timeskip
content:
Bleach has officially ended its TV anime franchise with the release of its final episode after 22 long years, and with it gives fans a look at how Ichigo Kurosaki and the others are now living ten years after the fight with Yhwach. It’s been a long wait for fans to see the final arc from Tite Kubo’s original manga to make it to screen, but Bleach: Thousand-Year Blood War kicked off that return a few years ago with four seasons taking on the massive final war for the fate of all three worlds.

Bleach: Thousand-Year Blood War has now ended its own four season run with its final episode, and it comes over ten years following the end of the original TV anime series. With the penultimate episode officially ending the long fight against Yhwach, the final episode of the anime then goes ten years into the future to reveal what life is like for Ichigo and the others as they prepare for what’s next in their lives. Check out the special ending for the grand finale below.

Bleach: Thousand-Year Blood War Anime Officially Ends With Episode 50 Timeskip

Bleach: Thousand-Year Blood War Episode 50 is titled “Death & Strawberry ,” and adapts the final two chapters from Tite Kubo’s original Bleach manga. Taking place ten years after the fight with Yhwach, the episode reveals what’s happened to everyone during all that time. Not only are a new set of Captains revealed for the Thirteen Court Guard Squads (including some former Captain favorites), the episode then reveals that Rukia has been newly crowned as Captain of Squad 13 with Renji being her Lieutenant. All the while a mysterious spiritual pressure starts to form.

Meanwhile, Ichigo and the others are gathering to watch Chad’s professional boxing fight. It’s revealed that Ichigo has married Orihime, and the two have had a child together named Kazui . It’s the same for Rukia and Renji, who have had a child together named Ichika. Kazui is revealed to not only have an affinity to see spirits like his mother and father have, but also quickly deals with the spiritual pressure as it forms. This turns out to have been the final remnants of Yhwach, and now he’s been fully dealt with for good. All three worlds are at peace.

Is This Really the End for Bleach ?

Bleach: Thousand-Year Blood War has ended its TV anime run, but there’s still much more of the franchise to celebrate in the near future. The franchise has announced it will be returning next year with a special “ Bleach Fes.” event in Japan to celebrate how far the anime has come in 22 years . This event will feature members of the voice cast and staff reflecting on the anime, and if we’re lucky it could be where the anime teases what’s coming next.

Because while the anime has completed its adaptation of Bleach ‘s original manga run, there are still other things that could be adapted. Kubo himself returned to series years after with an official one-shot that actually started a whole new arc against returning enemies from a new realm, Hell. If fans are lucky, we could see the anime return for more someday down the line.

What did you think of Bleach: Thousand-Year Blood War ‘s finale? Can you believe Bleach is really over after 22 years? Let us know all of your thoughts in the comments!

title: BLEACH Anime Ends 22-Year Run With Special Ending Movie After Thousand-Year Blood War Finale
content:
BLEACH anime has officially ended after a near 22-year run following the release of BLEACH: Thousand-Year Blood War – The Calamity Episode 50. The final episode released on October 27, 2026, while the original BLEACH anime debuted in 2004. To commemorate the conclusion, a special ending movie was released after the finale.

BLEACH: Thousand-Year Blood War has revealed a new “THE STORIES VISUAL – Final Battle” visual following the premiere of Episode 49, “THE BLADE.” The anime returned with the fourth and final cour, subtitled The Calamity , on July 25, before delaying the final two episodes to improve quality . It is set to run for 10 episodes, with Episode 9 releasing today. The series finale, Episode 50, will release on October 26.

You can see the new visual below.

Created by Tite Kubo, BLEACH was serialized in Weekly Shonen Jump from 2001 to 2016 and concluded with 74 volumes. The manga has exceeded 130 million copies in circulation worldwide, making it one of the best-selling manga series of all time.

The original anime adaptation aired from 2004 to 2012 and received four theatrical films. The franchise returned in 2022 with BLEACH: Thousand-Year Blood War , adapting the manga’s final arc. Its final part (Part 4) is set to release in July. Tite Kubo has confirmed it will include even more original material than the previous parts , expanding the manga’s final battles.

On a related note, BLEACH: Mirrors High revealed its protagonists in a new trailer, with the game featuring original character designs by Tite Kubo.

title: Yukari Kaneko's Hanarabeez Original Character Gets 3-Episode Short Anime
content:
The official YouTube channel of Shueisha 's Ribon magazine started streaming the first of three episodes for the short anime adaptation of manga artist Yukari Kaneko 's Hanarabeez original character, on Monday. The " Hanarabeez " anime's second episode will stream on November 9, and the third episode will premiere on November 24 at 12:00 noon JST.

The Ribon YouTube channel describes the short anime:

All the characters in this series are "teeth." Enjoy the laid-back, cute, and slightly surreal daily lives of these various "teeth."

Hana Satō and Yūki Urushiyama star in the short anime. Eagle Talon creator FROGMAN will also voice a character in the anime.

Benpineko ( Itsumo Wagamama Gama Ōji , MonHun Nikki Girigiri Airū-mura G , MonHun Nikki Girigiri Airū-mura Airū Kiki Ippatsu ) is directing the anime at DLE .

Additional staff members includes:

• Animation Director: Mamoru Suzuki

• Animation: Chieko Moriya, Chiaki Nishihara, Tu9Ne

• Production Assistant: Teppei Namikawa

• Recording Director: Yūsuke Watanabe

• Sound Effects: Yoko Sakurai (Swara Pro)

• Recording: Nobuto Kojima

• Sound Production: INSPION Edge

• Sound Production Manager: Reiko Takahashi

• Recording Studio: Three S Studio

• Recording Assistant: Ryō Hattori

Kaneko's Hanarabeez is one of the inaugural characters of Ribon magazine's "Charatan Labo" original character project , which launched in September 2025. Under the project, Ribon magazine publishes four-panel manga of original characters every month.

title: Black Clover Season 2 Preview Reveals First Look at the Fight Fans Waited 5 Years For
content:
Black Clover Season 2 has been working its way through the rematches against the Spade Kingdom’s Dark Triad, and the first look preview for the next episode has dropped the first look at one of the coolest fights yet as Magna steps into action. Black Clover Season 2 has thankfully returned to action against the Dark Triad after five long years of waiting for these fights to go down , and the episodes thus far have been pushing each of the Magic Knights to their respective limits against their strongest foes yet.

Black Clover Season 2 Episode 4 ended with a tease that Magna and Zora had made their way to the Spade Kingdom as Asta was fighting the now fused devil twins, and the first look at the next episode is setting up for Magna’s big fight. It’s his biggest moment in the series from Yuki Tabata’s original manga, and it’s the most anticipated fight for the second season overall as Magna takes on Dante. Check out the preview images for Black Clover Season 2 Episode 5 below.

Black Clover Season 2 Episode 5 Reveals First Look & Synopsis

Black Clover Season 2 Episode 5 is titled “The Best vs. The Worst,” and will be making its debut in Japan on October 31st, and will be streaming exclusively with Crunchyroll when it hits for fans in North America and other international territories. The episodes thus far have been packed to the brim with all sorts of notable fights as the arc jumps in between each of the members of the Dark Triad, but there’s been a renewed focus on Dante as Nacht had been facing off against the twins. With Asta taking them out of the picture, it’s time to take on Dante in full.

That’s what’s being teased by the synopsis for the episode on the anime’s official website too, “Asta rushes to Nacht’s aid, uniting with Liebe to confront Lilith. Meanwhile, Magna and Zora of the Black Bulls arrive to help Jack, who is battling Dante, the Dark Triad, who has reached 100% of his demonic power.” Magna’s debut in this second season has been especially looked forward to as his fight with Dante in the manga is the most unique that fans will see in the series from now on . And that’s even including the final arc.

What to Know for Magna vs. Dante

Magna’s fight against Dante was one of the big moments teased with the new opening sequence for Black Clover Season 2 , and the synopsis for the episode further reveals how this comes to be with the detailing of Magna’s newly developed spell for the occasion, “Dante appears confident despite his overwhelming magical power. However, Magna unleashes a new magic spell using a magic word he spent six months developing: ‘Underworld Flame Magic: Soul Chain Deathmatch.’” And this levels the playing field between the two.

It’s still not an easy fight however as the rest of the synopsis teases, “Even so, Dante, with his physical magic, remains a formidable opponent. But Magna, with the ‘guts’ that Yami acknowledged, clings to Dante!” It’s Magna’s biggest moment of the series that he’s been building to since the very beginning, so make sure to catch the episode when it hits. What are you hoping to see from the fight between Magna and Dante in Black Clover Season 2? Let us know all of your thoughts about it in the comments!

However, Magna unleashes a new magic spell using a magic word he spent six months developing: ‘Underworld Flame Magic: Soul Chain Deathmatch.’” And this levels the playing field between the two.

It’s still not an easy fight however as the rest of the synopsis teases, “Even so, Dante, with his physical magic, remains a formidable opponent. But Magna, with the ‘guts’ that Yami acknowledged, clings to Dante!” It’s Magna’s biggest moment of the series that he’s been building to since the very beginning, so make sure to catch the episode when it hits. What are you hoping to see from the fight between Magna and Dante in Black Clover Season 2? Let us know all of your thoughts about it in the comments!

title: Looney Tunes Voice Actor Eric Bauza Dies at 46
content:
The family of voice actor Eric Bauza announced on his Instagram account that he had suddenly died on Sunday. The announcement stated that there will be more details to come. Entertainment news website Variety reported that according to Los Angeles County Medical Examiner records, Bauza died at his home due to hypertensive cardiovascular disease. He was 46.

Bauza was born in Scarborough, Toronto on December 7, 1979. His first voice acting role was in The Ripping Friends in 2001, and his first major role was as the new voice of Stimpy in Ren & Stimpy "Adult Party Cartoon." He is perhaps best known for voicing many classic characters in the Looney Tunes franchise . He voiced Marvin the Martian in The Looney Tunes Show in 2011. He later voiced Bugs Bunny, Daffy Duck, Tweety, and more characters in the modern Looney Tunes Cartoons and video games for the franchise . In the 2021 Space Jam: A New Legacy film, Bauza voiced Daffy Duck, Porky Pig, Foghorn Leghorn, Elmer Fudd, and Marvin the Martian. In 2023, Bauza became the new voice of Buster Bunny in the Tiny Toons Looniversity reboot show. He also voiced characters in Avatar: The Last Airbender , Alvin and the Chipmunks: The Squeakquel , Scooby-Doo! Mystery Incorporated , and more. He played Diddy Kong and Toad General in The Super Mario Bros. Movie .

This year, Bauza reprised his role as Toad General in The Super Mario Galaxy Movie . He also played Mr. Mailbox, Worry Well, Couchy, Trashy, and Pee Flower in the horror film Buddy . In the recent Coyote vs. Acme film alone, Bauza voiced Bugs Bunny, Charlie Dog, Daffy Duck, Dr. Peter Lorre, Foghorn Leghorn, Gossamer, Pepé Le Pew, Porky Pig, Road Runner, Senator Elmer Fudd, and Tweety. His latest and last feature film role was in Forgotten Island , where he voiced Gen. Button Wutton and the mythological creature Sarangay. According to Variety, Bauza was in pre-production on two projects at the time of his death: as Daffy Duck in Bye Bye Bunny: A Looney Tunes Musical and as The Shogun King in The Dragon Masters .

In anime, Bauza is the English voice of Kenjirō Takōda in The Fable and Zigita Zogi the One Thousand and First in the second season of Ishura . Bauza also voiced Amadeus Cho in Avengers Confidential: Black Widow & Punisher , Two-Face in Batman Ninja , and Technovore/Ezekiel Stane in Iron Man: Rise of Technovore .

Bauza has won three Children's & Family Emmy Awards for Teen Titans Go! , Bugs Bunny Builders, and Looney Tunes Cartoons . He also received five nominations for Daytime Emmy Awards for his work on Looney Tunes Cartoons , Muppet Babies and The Adventures of Puss in Boots .

title: Eric Bauza’s Final Performance is Another Looney Tunes Film That Warner Bros. Originally Cancelled
content:
Eric Bauza, the modern voice of Looney Tunes icons such as Bugs Bunny and more has died at the age of 46 , and one of his final performances will be in a new Looney Tunes film that had been initially cancelled by Warner Bros. Discovery. Before Warner Bros. went through yet another merger with Paramount to form Skydance, its initial merger with Discovery had resulted in a number of new animated projects announced to be in the works that were subsequently shelved a few years later.

Some of these famous projects include the recently released The Day the Earth Blew Up: A Looney Tunes Movie and Coyote vs. Acme (which went on to box office success), but there was one other that had seemingly been cancelled forever. Bye Bye Bunny: A Looney Tunes Musical was seemingly cancelled back in 2022, but a recent update from Variety has revealed that Bauza was currently in pre-production on the film as of the time of his death. Meaning that there was a move towards release for the film once more.

Bye Bye Bunny: A Looney Tunes Musical Revealed to Be in Production Following Cancellation

Bye Bye Bunny: A Looney Tunes Musical was first announced to be in the works for a release with Cartoon Network and HBO Max in 2022 , and was subsequently cancelled alongside other animated projects like Batman: Caped Crusader, The Day The Earth Blew Up: A Looney Tunes Movie, Merry Little Batman and more. Notably many of these other cancelled projects eventually were saved and released through other distributors or streaming services, so it seems like it was going to be the same case for this Looney Tunes musical as well.

But unfortunately with Bauza passing away in the midst of the film’s pre-production, it’s not quite clear how far along the musical actually is. With the passing of the lead star behind the film, it’s not clear just how much voice work he had been able to record. This ultimately might lead to the film being shelved once more depending on how the newly formed Skydance decides to move forward with the Looney Tunes property (and its potentially in development projects) with the loss of their biggest voice star .

You Should Watch Coyote vs. Acme

For now, Bauza’s final performance as Bugs Bunny (and many other Looney Tunes icons) can be heard in the recently released Coyote vs. Acme , which the actor had been a great champion of while it was in limbo. When the film was originally scrapped for tax purposes by Warner Bros. Discovery and had no hope of release, Bauza often took as many opportunities as he could to have a distributor save the film from its fate such as when he took the stafe at the Annie Awards in 2023 .

Acting out a scene between Bugs Bunny and Daffy Duck, Bauza took a shot at Warner Bros. Discovery, “It could’ve been worse, Daffy. We could be Wile E. Coyote right now.” Which Bauza (as Daffy) then responded with, “I hate to be political, but release Coyote vs. Acme !” Bauza’s campaigning along with the rest of the team eventually did lead to the successful release of the film ( which is now available to buy or rent on digital stores ), and it proved that the Looney Tunes truly could kick off a new era.

Are you hoping to see Bye Bye Bunny: A Looney Tunes Musical release someday? Let us know all of your thoughts about it in the comments!

HT – Variety

title: The World's Strongest Witch Anime Casts Yukana, Azusa Tadokoro
content:
The official website for the anime of Mochimaru Sakaki 's The World's Strongest Witch: I'm Starting My Free Life in a World Where Only I Can See the Online Strategy Guide ( Sekai Saikyō no Majo, Hajimemashita : Watashi dake "Kōryaku Site" o Mireru Sekai de Jiyū ni Ikimasu ) light novel series revealed two new cast members for the anime on Monday. Both new characters will appear in the anime's fourth episode on Wednesday. The new cast members include ( Note: Character name romanizations are not confirmed. ):

When Lorna manifests a completely useless ability, she's labeled an embarrassment to her family and kicked out of the house. With no money or food, she's about to hit rock bottom. But then, she figures out how to use her supposedly worthless SSS-Rank skill, “Internet.” This cheat-level talent gives her the know-how to gather an unlimited amount of valuable items and easily acquire rare equipment. Armed with godlike knowledge, Lorna's free to do anything she wants! If only she could figure out what "lmfao" means…

The anime debuted in Japan on October 7. Crunchyroll streams the anime as it airs, and is also streaming an English dub .

The anime stars:

• Azusa Tachibana as Rona Hermit

• Fairouz Ai as Erimina

• Honoka Inoue as Eruna

• Kana Hanazawa as Aries Tear Bluemoon

• Maria Naganawa as Ruru Ru Rie

• Yūto Uemura voices Reinhardt Highwind

• Nana Mizuki as Yggdrasil

Jōji Furuta ( ēlDLIVE , Double Decker! Doug & Kirill , Bad Girl ) is directing the anime at the studios Bridge and Aisle . Shoji Yonemura ( Pokémon Journeys: The Series , One Piece 2013-onwards, Bad Girl ) is in charge of the series scripts. Yūki Morimoto ( Cardfight!! Vanguard GZ , Boarding School Juliet , Bad Girl ) is designing the characters.

HoneyWorks feat. HaKoniwalily perform the opening theme song "Eikyōryoku∞Idol" (Infinitely Influential Idol), and the group Rokudenashi perform the ending theme song "Hoshi o Muguru" (Traversing the Stars).
